subject: Atlas Health private deployment: readiness runway and cutover checklist
messages:
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@atlashealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Williams <cwilliams@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-04T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Kickoff: private deployment readiness + network questions

Naomi —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We want to lock in the readiness checklist for our private (VPC) deployment and make sure the network/security gates are clear before we pick a cutover date. High level asks from our infra team:

- A concrete list of VPC/peering requirements and IP ranges to allow
- Firewall/NAT egress policy expectations and required ports
- Certs/KMS handshake and any required CSR details

Can you share the runbook and anything we should validate on our side prior to the handoff? We are targeting a late-Feb window but flexible.

Attaching our current topology (see attachment).

— Rajiv
Ops, Atlas Health
(attachment: atlas-current-topology.png)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-04T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: private deployment readiness + network questions

Rajiv —

Thanks for the topology. I've put together an initial readiness runway plus a concise pre-cutover checklist (attached). Highlights below — happy to walk through in a short call.

Essentials for VPC/private deployment (summary):
- IP ranges: please reserve a /24 for the Redwood runtime and a /26 for the control plane VPN tunnel. Exact prefixes we will provide once we confirm the account CIDR.
- Peering and routes: simple static routes from your transit gateway to the Redwood subnet. No asymmetric routing; ensure return path to Redwood is via the peering attachment.
- Firewall: allow outbound TLS (443) from runtime hosts to our control-plane endpoints (listed in the attached CSV) and allow inbound only from our bastion IPs for initial debugging windows.
- Ports: 443 (control plane), 22 (bastion, restricted), and a short list of health/probe ports (we specify in the checklist).
- Certificates/KMS: we support customer-managed keys via KMS; we will request the public key or a signed CSR during provisioning.

Quick ask: can you confirm whether Atlas will terminate TLS at a load balancer inside the VPC or pass-through to our containers? That changes the cert step.

Attachments included: redwood-private-deploy-checklist.csv, atlas-network-topology-v2.png, cutover-runbook.md

If it's easier, Ben or Marissa can jump on a 30-minute run-through with your infra team.

— Naomi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-02-05T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: private deployment readiness + network questions

Looping in a couple notes from runtime side that are easy to miss during handoffs:

- Keep the MTU at 1500 across peering to avoid fragmentation with our GPU boxes (large payloads).
- We need stable NTP access; please allow outbound UDP/123 to pool.ntp.org or provide an internal NTP endpoint.
- KV cache syncs may create short bursts; plan burst capacity for egress if you have per-minute egress caps.

Also, if Atlas will run an internal ALB terminating TLS, we will expect a health check path (/redwood/health) reachable from runtime hosts over the internal network. If we terminate TLS instead, we'll coordinate key material exchange.

Ben
Runtime Ops, Redwood Dedicated
(attachment note: sample-health-check-config.json)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@atlashealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-06T14:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: private deployment readiness + network questions

Rajiv/Naomi —

Couple of deployment-level constraints from the orchestration side:

- VPN keepalive: we recommend 30s keepalives and a 3x retry before failover to avoid flapping during short network blips.
- CIDR plan: do not overlap Redwood-managed subnets; if Atlas prefers, provide a list of allowed CIDRs and we will map those to tenant routing.
- SNAT behavior: if you have strict egress policies, we can provide a NAT gateway on our side but it requires additional peering and IP blocks; flag if you want us to own SNAT.

Proposed next step: schedule a 45-minute alignment with Atlas networking, include a firewall engineer and cloud infra lead. I can share a minimal test plan (smoke tests for connectivity, health endpoints, certificate chaining) beforehand.

— Karthik
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Claire Williams <cwilliams@atlashealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-09T10:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: private deployment readiness + network questions

Hi team —

Thanks — we've reviewed the checklist and the attachments. A couple of clarifying items before we book the alignment call:

1) Atlas will terminate TLS at the internal ALB and will present certs. We will provide the public cert and our ALB SANs.
2) We can reserve a /24 for Redwood; need the exact IP blocks you will use for runtime instances (you mentioned you will provide).
3) Proposed cutover windows: Feb 25 22:00-01:00 UTC or Feb 28 02:00-05:00 UTC. The latter is preferred for our database maintenance window.

Can you confirm if the Feb 28 window works for Redwood's on-call and that the runbook includes rollback steps?

— Claire
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Atlas Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@atlashealth.com>, Claire Williams <cwilliams@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: private deployment readiness + network questions

Claire/Rajiv —

Feb 28 02:00-05:00 UTC is confirmed on Redwood's side. Our cutover runbook includes:

- Pre-cutover checklist (DNS TTLs, certs in place, health-check endpoints, smoke tests)
- Step-by-step cutover with timed checkpoints and ownership (we will provide the annotated runbook)
- Rollback criteria and automated rollback commands for the most common failure modes (certificate mismatch, healthcheck failures, significant error-rate increase)
- Post-cutover validation (latency SLO smoke, token telemetry sanity, quota checks)

I've attached the annotated cutover-runbook.md. Ben will own runtime checks; Karthik will own routing/VPN; Marissa will coordinate the console/account handoff and create the final access matrix.

Next actions:
- Atlas to share ALB certs + SANs and the reserved /24 by 2026-02-17
- Redwood to provide the exact runtime IPs and the annotated runbook by 2026-02-12
- 45-minute alignment call scheduled for 2026-02-18 15:00 UTC (calendar invite to follow)

We will also upload the checklist to the shared Drive link included above.

— Naomi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood-private-deploy-checklist.csv, cutover-runbook.md)
